source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide why Earth's position around the Sun matters for liquid water and habitability.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Earth is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: Too-hot or too-cold conditions do not satisfy the liquid-water condition for life as described in the chapter.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: temperature range -> liquid water can exist -> habitability becomes possible happens first, and that produces orbital distance.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Too-hot or too-cold conditions do not satisfy the liquid-water condition for life as described in the chapter is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: Earth is at the right distance from the Sun, where the temperature is neither too hot nor too cold, allowing water to exist in liquid form in the habitable zone. orbital distance -> temperature range -> liquid water can exist -> habitability becomes possible The learner correctly uses the chapter relationship: Earth is at the right distance from the Sun, where the temperature is neither too hot nor too cold, allowing water to exist in liquid form in the habitable zone. A planet is habitable whenever it has the label Blue Planet or is near Earth in space.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Why Earth supports life. The student must decide: Decide why Earth's position around the Sun matters for liquid water and habitability. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. Recalculate the key; do not copy source.key. Every option must be a claim that could answer the stem, and wrong options must be the same kind of answer as the key (a next term, a named process, or a row of the same shape). If the stem continues a number list, every option names a next term. Never write that naming or writing a term is what creates the list. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part
